title: Enterprise Contract Approval & Procurement Workflow (Finance, Legal, RevRec) - 2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose

This page documents the end-to-end enterprise contract approval and procurement workflow for Redwood Inference, and clarifies the interplay with revenue recognition (RevRec) and billing policy. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, Sales, and Product teams. The process below standardizes approvals, ownership, and triggers for invoicing and RevRec.

Scope

- Applies to all vendor and customer contracts, procurement requests, and SOWs that: 
  - create a legal obligation (customer contracts, vendor agreements, SOWs); or
  - result in capital or operational spend >= $5,000; or
  - impact revenue (pricing, billing cadence, delivery milestones).
- Excludes low-risk, pre-approved purchases under the petty cash policy (< $500).

High-level Principles

1. Single source of truth: all contracts and procurement requests must be initiated and tracked in the Contracts & Procurement queue in the Finance Portal (Jira project: FIN-PROC) and stored in the Agreements S3 bucket (s3://redwood-agreements).
2. Segregation of duties: requestor != approver != approver that signs on behalf of the company.
3. Risk-based review: monetary and legal-risk thresholds determine review level (see thresholds table below).
4. RevRec alignment: contract terms (delivery, acceptance, performance obligations) must include clear RevRec triggers to enable timely and GAAP-compliant revenue recognition.

Approval Thresholds & Required Approvals

| Amount (USD) | Finance Approval | Legal Review | CRO / Revenue Approval | CEO / Board Notice |
|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| < 5,000 | Auto-approved (ticket) | No | No | No |
| 5,000 - 50,000 | Finance Manager | Standard Legal Template check | No | No |
| 50,000 - 250,000 | Finance Director | Legal review (templates & redlines) | Revenue Ops review | Yes (email to execs)
| > 250,000 | VP Finance sign-off | Legal senior counsel sign-off | CFO & CRO sign-off | Yes (board-level summary)

Key Roles & Responsibilities

- Requestor: initiates FIN-PROC ticket, attaches redline request or template, business justification, budget code, and expected payment terms.
- Procurement Lead: validates vendor details, performs vendor risk and AML check (if applicable), completes PO creation.
- Finance Reviewer: checks budget availability, payment terms, tax implications, and RevRec treatment.
- Legal Counsel: reviews material terms (indemnities, data/privacy, IP, liability caps, termination, SLA). Uses the Contract Risk Matrix (link in Related Pages) to grade risk.
- Signatory: delegated signer per Authorization Matrix (Finance Portal > Delegations).
- RevRec Owner (Revenue Ops): maps contract to recognition schedule and books revenue events in the RevRec ledger.

Procedure: Customer Contracts & SOWs (step-by-step)

1. Pre-Sales / Sales Preparation
   - Use the approved Sales Contract Template for standard enterprise deals.
   - For pricing deviations>10% from list or non-standard billing cycles, attach variance justification and route for Revenue Ops review.

2. Sales submits FIN-PROC ticket with: customer legal name, template/SOW draft, effective date, pricing table, payment terms, fiscal billing code, required confidentiality level, assigned AE and AM.

3. Finance validates budget and billing code (target SLA: 24 business hours). If billing impact on RevRec, Revenue Ops is looped in.

4. Legal performs review and returns redlines (target SLA: 3 business days for standard terms, 10 business days for custom provisions).

5. Negotiation & Countersignature
   - Track all redlines in the FIN-PROC ticket.
   - For material changes affecting revenue recognition (e.g., milestone-based delivery, significant acceptance testing), Revenue Ops must sign off before countersign.
   - Final signatory executes via DocuSign. Signed doc is uploaded to s3://redwood-agreements/clients/<customer-org>/.

6. Post-signature
   - Finance issues invoice per billing schedule (see Billing & Invoicing section) and notifies Revenue Ops to create RevRec schedule.
   - Revenue Ops confirms contract mapping and posts the first recognition entry in the ledger within 3 business days of contract effective date.

Procedure: Vendor Procurement (step-by-step)

1. Requestor opens FIN-PROC ticket and selects type: Purchase Order, One-time Purchase, Contracted Services. Attach quotes, SOWs, and vendor risk forms.

2. Procurement Lead runs vendor onboarding checks: SBO (Supplier Business Overview), AML screen, security questionnaire if vendor handles customer data (target SLA: 2 business days for low-risk vendors).

3. Finance reviews PO, tax classification, payment method (ACH vs wire), and coding. If > $50k, Finance Director approval required.

4. Legal reviews vendor master agreements for terms that increase liability or data/privacy risk. If vendor will access customer data, require SCF (Security & Compliance Form) and DPA signed.

5. Sign-off and PO issuance: Procurement issues PO and attaches to FIN-PROC ticket; procurement team creates the PO in Coupa (or internal PO system) and confirms delivery expectations.

Billing & Invoicing Standards

- Standard payment terms: Net 30 for new customers (unless negotiated). Early payment discounts must be approved by VP Finance.
- Invoicing cadence: Monthly in arrears for subscription services unless contract specifies upfront or milestone billing.
- Invoices must reference the contract ID and FIN-PROC ticket. Submit invoices to billing@redwood.com; use the invoicing template below.

Inline Invoice Template (example)

{
  "invoice_number": "RWI-2026-000123",
  "contract_id": "RWI-CTR-2026-0456",
  "period_start": "2026-03-01",
  "period_end": "2026-03-31",
  "amount_due": "15000.00",
  "payment_terms": "Net 30"
}

Revenue Recognition (RevRec) Policy Alignment

- Revenue should be recognized when performance obligations are satisfied and collectibility is probable in accordance with ASC 606. For Redwood products this typically maps as: 
  - Hosted API (usage/subscription): recognized ratably over the service period (monthly/quarterly).
  - Dedicated/Private deployments with acceptance testing or milestone delivery: recognize on delivery/acceptance milestone.
  - Professional services (SOW): allocate and recognize as services are performed per percentage-of-completion or upon delivery depending on contract terms.

- Required RevRec metadata to capture in FIN-PROC ticket: contract_id, performance_obligations (list), billing_schedule, acceptance_criteria, estimated revenue allocation, and customer payment creditworthiness.

Controls & Audit Trail

- Every contract and procurement flow must include: FIN-PROC ticket ID, uploaded final executed contract, signatory name and DocuSign audit trail, PO number (if applicable), and RevRec mapping document.
- Monthly internal audit: Finance will run a contracts-to-ledger reconciliation to ensure all contracted revenues are recognized and all vendor liabilities are recorded. Discrepancies are remediated within the next month.

Exceptions & Escalations

- For urgent procurements (operational outages, incidents) use the Emergency Procurement path: email procurement@redwood.com with subject line "EMERGENCY PROC: <brief reason>". Emergency purchases require retroactive documentation in FIN-PROC within 3 business days and must be approved by VP Finance.
- Disputes on contract language escalate to Legal Ops; billing disputes escalate to Billing Ops (billing@redwood.com) with a target resolution SLA of 10 business days.

Operational Metrics & SLAs

- Finance validation SLA: 24 business hours for budget checks.
- Legal review SLA: 3 business days for standard templates; 10 business days for custom contracts.
- Vendor onboarding (low-risk): 2 business days.
- RevRec scheduling after signature: 3 business days.
